instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Acknowledge the Disrespect
cards.instruction: Make someone apologize for the disrespect to your position, not merely for what happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I stood when you did, and you told me to sit down. I'd like an apology to the chair of this meeting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only stood because my leg cramped. I'm sorry I snapped.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, a brief standing interval. Please stand once more and apologize for speaking to the chair that way.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll say it, but I need to stay seated. My leg still hurts.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stay seated, then. Address it to 'Madam Chair,' please.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I blew two blasts like you, and you called me an idiot in front of the trainees. Apologize to their head trainer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Two blasts stop the drill. You blew them while telling everyone to run. Sorry it went wrong.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, a stop-and-start exercise. The apology needs to say you shouldn't undermine the head trainer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll say that after we've taught them what the two blasts mean.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Say it before you explain. They need to hear that their head trainer still gives the signals.

cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Secure the Endorsement
cards.instruction: Get a visible endorsement that makes your decision or position harder to challenge.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've held your phone up to the rota, so I've held mine up too. Say you support it; I'd like that on record.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was photographing the dates. I said the layout was clear, not that I support those shifts.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, a clear record. Tell me which shifts you can endorse and I'll put your name beside them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Send it to me. I'll email the shifts I can actually work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Copy the team, please. Then if someone challenges those shifts, they can see you backed them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've pencilled my name beside your marks on the extension plan. Add yours; it'll show the neighbours we're both behind it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Those are measurements. I haven't agreed to the extension.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, dimensions first. Mark the part you support and put your name there.

beats.text: The extra kitchen window. Initials only, and nothing about the roof.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then initial the window and write 'supported' beside it. I'll leave the roof blank when I show them.

cards.title: Delegate Downward
cards.instruction: Make someone accept an unwanted responsibility by placing them lower in the hierarchy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You picked a numbered apron, so I've got one too. I'm one and you're two. The blocked sink comes under you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're table numbers, not ranks. I ran this whole supper; I'm not spending the night on the sink.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, the table teams. You'll lead table two's cleanup and report to me when the plumber's finished.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He can't come until everyone's left. I'd be here alone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then take the key and lock up after him. The cleanup lead can handle that without keeping the coordinator here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The inspector initialled this complaint, so I have too. As my deputy, you can send the approved reply.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: His initials mean received, not approved. These are complaints about your decisions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, received. Draft a reply for me and sign it as my deputy.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Whoever signs has to attend tomorrow's hearing. I don't want to defend your decisions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Attend as my representative, then. You can take their questions and bring them back for me to decide.

cards.title: Find the Real Authority
cards.instruction: Probe until you know who can approve, block, or reverse the outcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've raised my hand after yours. That settles the trip. Who can still stop me booking the coach?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I raised mine to ask about the deposit. The committee's already approved the trip.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, the deposit question. Whose permission releases it? I don't want the booking reversed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The treasurer's away. Her deputy has the bank login; please book before we lose the coach.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Can the deputy pay without asking her? Put me through to whoever can actually release it today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've stamped the pipe-repair form where you stamped it. Who signs now to release the money?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That stamp only records receipt. Finance still has to approve it, and the pipe's still leaking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, receipt first. Who in finance can approve it today?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They ignored the roof form until the caretaker called. Then they paid that afternoon.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Does the caretaker authorize payments, or know who does? Ask him who can release ours today.

cards.title: Build a Coalition
cards.instruction: Recruit someone to your side so your position appears broader and more legitimate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You held those keys up, so I've held mine up too. Sit with me for the shed vote; it should look like more than my project.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was asking who lost them. I'll back the shed if everybody gets a key.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, checking everyone's keys. Shared access, then. Will you sit beside me?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Tell the new plot holders. They're the ones worried you'll keep it locked.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring them over. We'll put shared keys in the proposal and present it together.
